## Running and Debugging Tests

### Building Tests
```bash
# Build all tests
cd build && make

# Build specific test suite
cd build && make libslic3r_tests

# Build and run tests
cd build && make && ctest
```

### Running Tests

#### Essential Test Execution Patterns
```bash
# REQUIRED: Random order with assertion warnings (best practice)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Run all tests with verbose output via CTest
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

# Run specific test suite with best practices
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Filter tests with specific tags
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry]" --order rand

# Filter by test name patterns
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "*geometry*" --order rand

# Exclude tests (negation)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "~[Performance]" --order rand

# Combine filters: (Geometry AND Config) OR Algorithm
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry][Config],[Algorithm]" --order rand

# List available tests, tags, and reporters
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tags  
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-reporters

# Debug failing tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --break    # Break into debugger on failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --success  # Show passing tests too
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --durations yes  # Show timing info

# Abort on first failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --abort

# Test sharding for parallel execution (MUST share random seed)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 3 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
wait  # Wait for all to complete
```

```bash
# Different output formats for CI systems
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console     # Default human-readable
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter compact     # Minimal output
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter xml         # Catch2 XML format
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter junit       # JUnit XML (widely supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter tap         # Test Anything Protocol
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter teamcity    # TeamCity integration

# Multiple reporters simultaneously (if supported)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --reporter console --reporter junit::out=results.xml
```

### Test Output Control
The custom `VerboseConsoleReporter` provides enhanced output:
- Test case start/end notifications with timing
- Section execution tracking
- Color-coded success/failure indicators
- Duration reporting for performance analysis

## Test Data Management

### Using TEST_DATA_DIR
All test data is accessible via the `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition:

```cpp
std::string mesh_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/20mm_cube.obj";
std::string config_path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/test_config/printer.ini";
```

### Available Test Assets

#### 3D Models
- **Basic shapes**: `20mm_cube.obj`, `pyramid.obj`, `sphere.obj`
- **Complex geometry**: `extruder_idler.obj`, `ipadstand.obj`, `bridge.obj`
- **Edge cases**: `cube_with_hole.obj`, `sloping_hole.obj`, `small_dorito.obj`

#### File Format Tests
- **STL variants**: ASCII/binary, different line endings, Unicode names
- **3MF files**: Multi-material, complex assemblies
- **Configuration files**: Various printer/material profiles

#### Test Utilities
The `Test` namespace provides helper functions:
```cpp
using namespace Slic3r::Test;

// Load standard test meshes
TriangleMesh mesh = mesh(TestMesh::cube_20x20x20);

// Standard test configurations
DynamicPrintConfig config = config(TestConfig::PLA_default);
```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

## Performance Considerations

### Compilation Optimizations
```cpp
// In CMakeLists.txt or as preprocessor definition
#define CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE  // 20% faster compilation, disables some features

// For faster test iteration during development
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION  // Workaround for VS2017 raw string bug
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

### Memory Leak Detection
```cpp
// For Windows builds - detects memory leaks
#define CATCH_CONFIG_WINDOWS_CRTDBG  // Must be defined for whole build
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp
    test_new_feature.cpp  # Add here
)
```

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"
    DISCOVERY_MODE PRE_TEST  # or POST_BUILD
    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

# Test sharding for parallel execution
include(CatchShardTests)  # If available
catch_shard_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_hollowing.cpp)
endif()

# Platform-specific tests
if(WIN32)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_windows_specific.cpp)
elseif(UNIX)
    target_sources(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE test_unix_specific.cpp)
endif()

# Compiler-specific workarounds
if(MSVC)
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION)
endif()

# Fast compile mode for development
if(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE STREQUAL "Debug")
    target_compile_definitions(${_TEST_NAME}_tests PRIVATE CATCH_CONFIG_FAST_COMPILE)
endif()
```

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp
// OrcaSlicer is on Catch2 v3.11.0 - all of these ARE available:
// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

// v3 notes to remember:
// - String matcher is "ContainsSubstring" (v2's "Contains" no longer exists)
// - Sections can still be re-run if a later section fails (unchanged from v2)
```

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

#### CI/CD Integration
```bash
# Essential CI test command
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter junit::out=results.xml

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --durations yes
```

name: cmake-file-edit-forces-full-rebuild
description: "Editing sources.cmake, or adding a file to a globbed directory such as a new AgentUI skill, after a commit re-runs CMake, which bakes the new HEAD into -DGIT_COMMIT_HASH on every compile line, so ninja rebuilds all ~970 steps."

2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

2026-11-02 (connection-skill worktree): adding two new `AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md` files did the same. The jusprin_web target globs that tree, so the build printed "GLOB mismatch!", re-ran CMake and started 945 steps for jusprin_web + agent_bridge_tests + shell_integration_harness.

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake`, and new skill or other globbed files, before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).
# GUI-free contract tests for fork-owned JusPrin data structures that carry no
# wx or Orca types. The sources under test are compiled directly into the test
# binary, so nothing here links libslic3r_gui.
add_executable(jusprin_tests
    test_filament_chip_model.cpp
    test_printer_facts_store.cpp
    test_host_locale.cpp
    test_home_snapshot.cpp
    test_project_status.cpp
    test_home_host.cpp
    test_onboarding_model.cpp
    test_printer_names.cpp
    test_host_lanes.cpp
    test_installed_models.cpp
    test_viewport_tool_strip.cpp
    test_left_pane_model.cpp
    test_project_pane_model.cpp
    test_print_issues.cpp
    test_load_facts.cpp
    test_check_print_report.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/FilamentChipModel.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/LeftPaneModel.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ProjectPaneModel.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/CheckPrintReportModel.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/PrinterFactsStore.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/LoadFacts.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeSnapshot.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/ProjectStatus.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/HomeHost.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OnboardingModel.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/PrinterNames.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/HostLanes.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/InstalledModels.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Canvas/ViewportToolStripLayout.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueContext.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout.cpp
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrintIssues/PrintIssue.cpp
)

target_compile_definitions(jusprin_tests PRIVATE
    JUSPRIN_SOURCE_DIR=R"\(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}\)"
)
target_include_directories(jusprin_tests PRIVATE
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/src
    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/deps_src
)
# test_common carries the macOS framework link (CoreFoundation) that
# HostLocale.hpp needs there; on Windows and Linux it adds nothing but the
# shared test defines.
target_link_libraries(jusprin_tests PRIVATE test_common Catch2WithMain nlohmann_json)

orcaslicer_discover_tests(jusprin_tests)

# The printer form's plates and filaments, read from the packaged profiles by
# OrcaSlicer's own preset loader, and the Preferences window's settings, read
# from and written to OrcaSlicer's AppConfig: this links libslic3r, but no GUI.
add_executable(jusprin_profile_tests
    test_setup_options.cpp
    test_preferences_settings.cpp

---
name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

"""Splits the -U0 diff of the given files into the email-door hunks and the
OrcaSlicer-import hunks, by keywords. Prints mixed or unclassified hunks."""
import re, subprocess, sys
IMPORT = re.compile(r"import_result|ImportResult|importResult|import_retry|import_continue|choose_orca|picked_orca|ImportItem|OrcaImport|orca_import|retry_orca|finish_orca|import_orca_files|import_result_lines|preset_collection|PresetCollection|detect_orca|OrcaProfileSource|orca_account|scan_orca|dirdlg|wxDirDialog|Orca copy|filaments? imported|OrcaSlicer folder|found|glyph-check|glyph-warning|CheckGlyph|WarningGlyph|importStatus|onboarding-import|ImportResultItem|presets\.printers\.empty|source\.presets|to_string\(OrcaImportItem|OrcaPresetFiles|failed items|Imported from OrcaSlicer|need attention|own files were not changed|its base profile|couldn.t be read|account_folder")
mode = sys.argv[1]
root = sys.argv[2]
out = {'door': [], 'import': []}
for path in sys.argv[3:]:
    diff = subprocess.run(['git', '-C', root, 'diff', '-U0', '--', path], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    head, _, rest = diff.partition('\n@@')
    hunks = ['@@' + h for h in ('\n@@' + rest).split('\n@@')[1:]] if rest else []
    for h in hunks:
        body = '\n'.join(l for l in h.splitlines()[1:])
        changed = [l for l in h.splitlines()[1:] if l[:1] in '+-']
        imp = [l for l in changed if IMPORT.search(l)]
        kind = 'import' if imp and len(imp) == len(changed) else 'door' if not imp else 'mixed'
        if kind == 'mixed' or mode == 'show':
            print(f'== {path} [{kind}]\n{h}\n')
        out.setdefault(kind, []).append((head, h))
print({k: len(v) for k, v in out.items()}, file=sys.stderr)
EOF

Let the JusPrin account sign in by email inside the app

CloudSignIn gains an Email phase beside the browser sign-in. The app
asks the server how an address signs in (POST /ent/jusprin/v2/auth/email):

six-digit code by email. A correct code or password brings the same
OAuth token the browser sign-in brings, so it is checked and stored by
the same begin_check. A wrong or expired code, too many tries and a
wrong password stay on their step for the person to act on; any other
answer ends the sign-in with the generic "couldn't sign you in".

(function(){
  const tag = (location.pathname.includes('agent') ? 'agent' : 'home') + (new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('panel') || '');
  const base = 'http://127.0.0.1:8766';
  const post = (q, body) => fetch(base + '/log?page=' + tag + q, {method: 'POST', body});
  async function tick() {
    try {
      const t = await (await fetch(base + '/cmd?page=' + tag)).text();
      if (t) { let out; try { out = await eval(t); } catch (e) { out = 'ERR ' + e; } await post('', 'RESULT ' + String(out)); }
    } catch (e) {}
    setTimeout(tick, 300);
  }
  tick();
  const wrap = setInterval(() => {
    if (window.__jusprinBridge && window.wx) {
      clearInterval(wrap);
      const d = window.__jusprinBridge.deliver.bind(window.__jusprinBridge);
      window.__jusprinBridge.deliver = (e) => { if (e.type === 'state') window.__last = e.payload; post('&env=' + e.type, 'IN ' + JSON.stringify(e.payload).slice(0, 3000)); return d(e); };
      const p = window.wx.postMessage.bind(window.wx);
      window.wx.postMessage = (j) => { try { const m = JSON.parse(j); post('&env=' + m.type, 'OUT ' + JSON.stringify(m.payload).slice(0, 500)); } catch (e) {} return p(j); };
    }
  }, 20);
  window.clickText = (t) => {
    const all = [...document.querySelectorAll('button,summary')];
    const b = all.find(x => x.textContent.trim() === t || x.getAttribute('aria-label') === t) || all.find(x => x.textContent.trim().startsWith(t));
    if (!b) return 'no button ' + t + ' among ' + all.map(x => x.textContent.trim()).filter(Boolean).slice(0, 30).join(' | ');
    b.click(); return 'clicked ' + t + (b.disabled ? ' (disabled)' : '');
  };
  window.sendAgent = (type, payload) => window.wx.postMessage(JSON.stringify({protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge', version:1, id:'d-'+Date.now(), type, payload})) || 'sent';
  window.text = () => document.body.innerText.slice(0, 1500);
})();
</script>

content.text: Now the driver script. Each run launches the built app on an empty data folder pointed at the local server, walks the door, and captures the app window at each state.

input.content:
#!/bin/zsh
# e2e.sh <light|dark> <code|password>
# The built app on an empty data folder, signed in by email against the local
# gateway (localhost:3534), with a screenshot of the window at each door state.
D=${0:A:h}; cd $D
APP=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
theme=$1; path=$2
SHOTS=$D/../shots/door; mkdir -p $SHOTS
R=$D/e2e-$theme-$path; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R/JusPrin
print '{"jusprin_server": {"base_url": "http://localhost:3534"}}' > $R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf
: > drive.log
ARGS=(--datadir $R/JusPrin); [[ $theme == dark ]] && ARGS+=(-AppleInterfaceStyle Dark)
JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/agent.html \
  $APP $ARGS > $D/e2e-$theme-$path.out 2>&1 &
P=$!
trap 'kill $P 2>/dev/null' EXIT

js(){ ./drive.sh home "$1" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //'; }
# until <name> <js condition>: polls the page for up to 30 s.
until_true(){ for i in {1..60}; do [[ $(js "String(Boolean($2))") == true ]] && { echo "ok $1"; return 0; }; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "TIMEOUT $1: $(js 'JSON.stringify({signIn: __last?.onboarding.signIn, email: __last?.onboarding.email, err: __last?.onboarding.signInError})')"; return 1; }
shot(){ sleep 0.8; screencapture -x -o -l $(./winid $P) $SHOTS/$theme-$1.png && echo "shot $theme-$1"; }
EMAIL=__last?.onboarding.email

for i in {1..120}; do grep -q "^home state" drive.log && break; sleep 0.5; done
until_true welcome "__last?.onboarding.step === 'welcome'" || exit 1
js "window.resizeTo && 'ready'" > /dev/null
shot 13a-rest

if [[ $path == code ]]; then
  # States the real app cannot reach here: the browser wait needs Continue
  # with Google, which this Mac must not press, and the v1 line a v1 import.
  js "fake({signIn: 'browser'})"; shot 12d-browser-wait-delivered
  js "fake({signIn: 'idle', v1Imported: true})"; shot 13a-v1-line-delivered
  js "fake({v1Imported: false})" > /dev/null

  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true code-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 12b-code
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '000000')"
  until_true wrong-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-wrong-code
  # The ten-minute expiry, as Redis does it.
  docker exec email-sign-in-redis-1 sh -c "redis-cli --scan --pattern '*sign_in:code:alex@example.com' | xargs -r redis-cli DEL" > /dev/null
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '111111')"
  until_true expired-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'expired_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-expired-code
  js "clickText('Send a new code')"
  until_true code-resent "$EMAIL?.codeResent === true && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  sleep 1; CODE=$(../latest_code.sh 1m); echo "emailed code read from the local mail backend (${#CODE} digits)"
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$CODE')"
else
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true password-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'password' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 13b-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', 'not the password')"; js "clickText('Sign in')"
  until_true wrong-password "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_password'" || exit 1
  shot 13b-wrong-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', '$(cat ../test-password)')" > /dev/null; js "clickText('Sign in')"
fi
until_true signed-in "__last?.onboarding.accountEmail === 'alex@example.com'" || exit 1
shot signed-in-$path
js "JSON.stringify({signIn: __last.onboarding.signIn, err: __last.onboarding.signInError, step: __last.onboarding.step})"
python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('$R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf')); a=c.get('jusprin_agent', {}); print('saved', sorted(k for k in a if 'jusprin' in k))"

Show what an OrcaSlicer import brought, item by item

Import on the Printers step used to ask yes or no in a dialog for each
name JusPrin already had, then said nothing about what it skipped. Now
a result screen follows it, one line per printer and process preset,
with the filaments counted:

- "Imported";
- "Imported as '<name> (Orca copy)'" when JusPrin had the name;
- "Not imported · <reason>": the file couldn't be read, has no version,
  isn't a preset, or names a base profile JusPrin lacks.

"Continue" leaves for Home, or for the add-printer form when no printer
came; "Retry failed items" imports the failed ones again. When no
OrcaSlicer folder is found beside JusPrin's, the add-printer form offers
"Import from an OrcaSlicer folder…", a folder picker that takes
OrcaSlicer's data folder, its user folder, an account folder or a
machine folder.

OrcaSlicer's PresetBundle::import_presets is unchanged. OrcaImport.cpp
reads each file first and gives a taken name a renamed copy in a temp
folder, so import_presets has nothing to ask; what it reports imported
settles the rest. OrcaSlicer's own files are only read. Detection moves
into the same GUI-free file, with tests.
EOF

Sign in by email from Home in the --fresh-example harness

After the first launch reaches Home, the agent card signs in by email
against a stand-in JusPrin server on a loopback port: the address, a
wrong code that stays on the code step with four tries left, then the
right code, which brings the account. The harness checks each request
the app sent.
EOF

# Global Claude Code Rules

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Throws and log lines may name Orca; they never reach the model.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

- [Before running or concluding](evidence-before-handing-kenneth-a-decision.md) — **write the question and who holds the answer first: search, logs, one observation; experiments last.**
- [Trace a rule to Kenneth's words](trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words.md) — briefs reword rules stricter; find his words and why before saying "your rule".
- [POC branch](jusprin-v2-poc-rebase-not-merge.md) — rebase the fork's commits, never merge.
- [Rebase risk](fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming.md) — three checks before claiming it.
- [Shell phase 1](jusprin-shell-phase-1-design.md) — hide the tab strip, don't reparent Plater.
- [Teardown crash](orca-inherited-teardown-crash.md) — exit segfault in ~GLCanvas3D; inherited.

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Throws and log lines may name Orca; they never reach the model.

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.

- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

#!/bin/zsh
# e2e.sh <light|dark> <code|password>
# The built app on an empty data folder, signed in by email against the local
# gateway (localhost:3534), with a screenshot of the window at each door state.
D=${0:A:h}; cd $D
APP=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/first-run-flow-f7be35/build/arm64/src/Release/OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer
theme=$1; path=$2
SHOTS=$D/../shots/door; mkdir -p $SHOTS
R=$D/e2e-$theme-$path; rm -rf $R; mkdir -p $R/JusPrin
print '{"jusprin_server": {"base_url": "http://localhost:3534"}}' > $R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf
: > drive.log
ARGS=(--datadir $R/JusPrin); [[ $theme == dark ]] && ARGS+=(-AppleInterfaceStyle Dark)
JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/home.html JUSPRIN_AGENT_DEV_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/agent.html \
  $APP $ARGS > $D/e2e-$theme-$path.out 2>&1 &
P=$!
trap 'kill $P 2>/dev/null' EXIT

js(){ ./drive.sh home "$1" | sed 's/^home  RESULT //'; }
# until <name> <js condition>: polls the page for up to 30 s.
until_true(){ for i in {1..60}; do [[ $(js "String(Boolean($2))") == true ]] && { echo "ok $1"; return 0; }; sleep 0.5; done
  echo "TIMEOUT $1: $(js 'JSON.stringify({signIn: __last?.onboarding.signIn, email: __last?.onboarding.email, err: __last?.onboarding.signInError})')"; return 1; }
shot(){ sleep 0.8; screencapture -x -o -l $(./winid $P) $SHOTS/$theme-$1.png && echo "shot $theme-$1"; }
EMAIL=__last?.onboarding.email

for i in {1..120}; do grep -q "^home state" drive.log && break; sleep 0.5; done
until_true welcome "__last?.onboarding.step === 'welcome'" || exit 1
js "window.resizeTo && 'ready'" > /dev/null
shot 13a-rest

if [[ $path == code ]]; then
  # States the real app cannot reach here: the browser wait needs Continue
  # with Google, which this Mac must not press, and the v1 line a v1 import.
  js "fake({signIn: 'browser'})"; shot 12d-browser-wait-delivered
  js "fake({signIn: 'idle', v1Imported: true})"; shot 13a-v1-line-delivered
  js "fake({v1Imported: false})" > /dev/null

  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true code-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'code' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 12b-code
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '000000')"
  until_true wrong-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-wrong-code
  # The ten-minute expiry, as Redis does it.
  docker exec email-sign-in-redis-1 sh -c "redis-cli --scan --pattern '*sign_in:code:alex@example.com' | xargs -r redis-cli DEL" > /dev/null
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '111111')"
  until_true expired-code "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'expired_code'" || exit 1
  shot 12c-expired-code
  js "clickText('Send a new code')"
  until_true code-resent "$EMAIL?.codeResent === true && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  sleep 1; CODE=$(../latest_code.sh 1m); echo "emailed code read from the local mail backend (${#CODE} digits)"
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Sign-in code\"]', '$CODE')"
else
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Email\"]', 'alex@example.com')"; js "clickText('Continue with email')"
  until_true password-step "$EMAIL?.step === 'password' && !$EMAIL?.busy" || exit 1
  shot 13b-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', 'not the password')"; js "clickText('Sign in')"
  until_true wrong-password "$EMAIL?.refusal === 'wrong_password'" || exit 1
  shot 13b-wrong-password
  js "typeInto('input[aria-label=\"Password\"]', '$(cat ../test-password)')" > /dev/null; js "clickText('Sign in')"
fi
until_true signed-in "__last?.onboarding.accountEmail === 'alex@example.com'" || exit 1
shot signed-in-$path
js "JSON.stringify({signIn: __last.onboarding.signIn, err: __last.onboarding.signInError, step: __last.onboarding.step})"
python3 -c "import json; c=json.load(open('$R/JusPrin/JusPrin2.conf')); a=c.get('jusprin_agent', {}); print('saved', sorted(k for k in a if 'jusprin' in k))"

90	{

92	    // Names this import takes, so two renamed copies never share one.
93	    std::set<std::pair<Kind, std::string>> taken;
94	    std::vector<nlohmann::json> contents;
95	    for (const std::string& file : files) {
96	        OrcaImportItem item;
97	        item.source = item.file = file;
98	        const fs::path path     = fs::u8path(file);
99	        item.kind               = kind_of_folder(path);
100	        item.name               = path.stem().u8string();
101	        std::optional<nlohmann::json> json = read_json(path);
102	        if (!json) {
103	            item.outcome = OrcaImportItem::Outcome::NotImported;
104	            item.reason  = OrcaImportItem::Reason::Unreadable;
105	        } else {
106	            if (const std::string name = string_value(*json, "name"); !name.empty())
107	                item.name = name;
108	            const bool is_preset = json->contains("printer_settings_id") || json->contains("print_settings_id") ||
109	                                   json->contains("filament_settings_id");
110	            if (string_value(*json, "version").empty())
111	                item.reason = OrcaImportItem::Reason::NoVersion;
112	            else if (!is_preset)
113	                item.reason = OrcaImportItem::Reason::NotAPreset;
114	            if (item.reason != OrcaImportItem::Reason::None)
115	                item.outcome = OrcaImportItem::Outcome::NotImported;
116	            taken.insert({item.kind, item.name});
117	        }
118	        items.push_back(std::move(item));
119	        contents.push_back(json ? std::move(*json) : nlohmann::json());
120	    }

122	    for (size_t index = 0; index < items.size(); ++index) {
123	        OrcaImportItem& item = items[index];
124	        if (item.outcome != OrcaImportItem::Outcome::Pending)
125	            continue;
126	        nlohmann::json& json = contents[index];
127	        item.base            = string_value(json, "inherits");
128	        const bool in_batch  = std::any_of(items.begin(), items.end(), [&](const OrcaImportItem& other) {
129	            return &other != &item && other.kind == item.kind && other.name == item.base;
130	        });
131	        if (!item.base.empty() && !in_batch && !catalog.has_base(item.kind, item.base)) {
132	            item.outcome = OrcaImportItem::Outcome::NotImported;
133	            item.reason  = OrcaImportItem::Reason::MissingBase;
134	            continue;

136	        if (!catalog.has(item.kind, item.name))

138	
139	        std::string renamed = item.name + " (Orca copy)";
140	        for (int copy = 2; catalog.has(item.kind, renamed) || taken.count({item.kind, renamed}) != 0; ++copy)
141	            renamed = item.name + " (Orca copy " + std::to_string(copy) + ")";
142	        taken.insert({item.kind, renamed});
143	        json["name"]                    = renamed;
144	        json[settings_id_key(item.kind)] = renamed;
145	        // Numbered, not named: a preset name can hold characters a file name cannot.
146	        const fs::path copy = staging / (std::to_string(index) + ".json");
147	        std::ofstream  stream(copy);
148	        stream << json.dump(4);
149	        if (!stream)
150	            throw std::runtime_error("Could not write the renamed copy " + copy.u8string());
151	        item.file       = copy.u8string();
152	        item.renamed_to = renamed;
153	    }
154	    return items;
155	}
156	
157	void settle_orca_import(std::vector<OrcaImportItem>& items, const std::vector<std::string>& imported)
158	{
159	    for (OrcaImportItem& item : items) {
160	        if (item.outcome != OrcaImportItem::Outcome::Pending)
161	            continue;
162	        if (std::find(imported.begin(), imported.end(), item.file) != imported.end()) {
163	            item.outcome = OrcaImportItem::Outcome::Imported;
164	        } else {
165	            item.outcome = OrcaImportItem::Outcome::NotImported;
166	            item.reason  = OrcaImportItem::Reason::NotLoaded;
167	        }
168	    }
169	}
170	
171	OrcaPresetFiles scan_orca_presets(const fs::path& account_folder)
172	{
173	    OrcaPresetFiles presets;
174	    const auto scan = [&](const char* subfolder, std::vector<std::string>& names) {
175	        std::error_code error;
176	        const fs::path  folder = account_folder / subfolder;
177	        if (!fs::is_directory(folder, error))
178	            return;
179	        std::vector<fs::path> files;
180	        for (const fs::directory_entry& entry : fs::directory_iterator(folder, error))
181	            if (entry.is_regular_file(error) && entry.path().extension() == ".json")
182	                files.push_back(entry.path());
183	        std::sort(files.begin(), files.end());
184	        for (const fs::path& file : files) {
185	            names.push_back(file.stem().u8string());
186	            presets.files.push_back(file.u8string());
187	        }
188	    };
189	    // Base machine profiles first, then their material and process children.
190	    scan(kPrinterFolder, presets.printers);
191	    scan(kFilamentFolder, presets.filaments);
192	    scan(kProcessFolder, presets.processes);
193	    return presets;
194	}
195	
196	std::optional<fs::path> orca_account_folder(const fs::path& orca_root)
197	{
198	    std::string configured;
199	    const fs::path config = orca_root / "OrcaSlicer.conf";
200	    std::error_code error;
201	    if (fs::is_regular_file(config, error)) {
202	        std::optional<nlohmann::json> json = read_config(config);
203	        if (!json)
204	            return std::nullopt;
205	        const auto app = json->find("app");
206	        if (app != json->end() && app->is_object())
207	            configured = string_value(*app, "preset_folder");
208	    }
209	
210	    const fs::path user = orca_root / kUserFolder;
211	    if (!configured.empty())
212	        return user / configured;
213	    fs::path        newest = user / kDefaultFolder;
214	    fs::file_time_type written{};
215	    for (const fs::directory_entry& account : fs::directory_iterator(user, error)) {
216	        for (const fs::directory_entry& item : fs::directory_iterator(account.path() / kPrinterFolder, error)) {
217	            if (item.path().extension() != ".json")
218	                continue;
219	            if (const fs::file_time_type time = item.last_write_time(error); time > written) {
220	                written = time;
221	                newest  = account.path();
222	            }
223	        }
224	        error.clear();
225	    }
226	    return newest;
227	}
228	
229	std::optional<fs::path> orca_account_folder_for_pick(const fs::path& picked)
230	{
231	    std::error_code error;
232	    if (fs::is_directory(picked / kUserFolder, error))
233	        return orca_account_folder(picked);
234	    if (has_json_files(picked / kPrinterFolder) || has_json_files(picked / kFilamentFolder) ||
235	        has_json_files(picked / kProcessFolder))
236	        return picked;
237	    if (picked.filename() == kPrinterFolder && has_json_files(picked))
238	        return picked.parent_path();
239	    // The user folder: its account folders hold the presets.
240	    if (picked.filename() == kUserFolder)
241	        return orca_account_folder(picked.parent_path());
242	    return std::nullopt;
243	}
244

- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. - workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- plugin-authoring: Make a mod: a change to Claude's own interface or behaviour, such as a panel or pane that stays beside the chat and updates, a band, status line, toast, slash command, or hook on tool calls. Use to make, change or debug a mod or its hooks module.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
